title: The four pillars of AI governance
oneliner: Enterprises pay a premium for AI that is explainable, responsible, compliant and secure, and observable - those four are the governance framework.
says: Why do enterprises pay a high premium for AI projects? Four reasons, which together form the AI governance framework: explainability (the model must be transparent about why it answers as it does), responsible AI (it must not behave weirdly, get exploited by vulnerabilities, or respond badly), compliance and security, and observability of the models and projects.
explained: Each pillar answers a different stakeholder's fear. Explainability answers the regulator and the customer: 'why did the system say that?' Responsible AI answers the public and the legal team: the system stays within acceptable behavior even under attack. Compliance and security answer the auditors: data handling, access, and the rules of your industry. Observability answers the engineering team: you cannot fix or improve what you cannot see.

The premium point is the one to remember. Governance is not a tax on AI projects - it is most of what an enterprise is buying. A demo model is cheap; a model that a bank can defend to its regulator is the expensive part. This is why his Season 2 platform series spends entire episodes on evaluation and centralized registries: governance is an architecture, not a slide deck (not just slides and promises).
takeaway: When scoping AI work, price the governance in from day one - explainability, responsible behavior, compliance, observability are the deliverable, not overhead.
